**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — EXCLUSIVITY**

**Where:** § 7.2 (p0026), read against § 12.3 (p0044).

**Issue:** "*7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.*"

This is a disclose-and-match gate on our ability to source elsewhere — a de facto exclusivity plus most-favoured-customer commitment binding us. It has no category limit, no time limit, and no performance-based exit, which sits at the walk-away end of the playbook. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or MFC commitment, and § 2.2's precedence ladder does not resolve conflicts internal to the Agreement.

**Resolution:** Deleted p0026 (preferred position: no exclusivity obligation on Customer). Nothing else in the document binds us — the remaining "exclusive" references relate to the non-exclusive licence grant (§ 13.1), remedies (§§ 19.4, 21.4, 30.2), and jurisdiction (§§ 28.1–28.2). The fallback (defined category, 12 months, automatic termination on missed service levels or delivery dates) is offered in the comment as a negotiating position.
